slides.headline: THEY LEFT 'CHATGPT.COM' IN THEIR OWN REPORT
slides.subline: AND THAT'S NOT THE WORST PART

slides.headline: FOUR FAKE REPORTS FROM A BILLION-DOLLAR FIRM
slides.body: PwC is one of the four biggest consulting firms on earth. They put out four reports between 2024 and 2026, all full of AI lies and fake sources

slides.headline: THEY CITED A TEENAGER WITH 280 FOLLOWERS
slides.body: One report cited a teenager's Medium blog with 280 followers as proof for a JPMorgan AI story. The kid was their source for one of the world's biggest banks

slides.headline: THE STORY HAPPENED BEFORE CHATGPT EXISTED
slides.body: The JPMorgan project was real, from 2017. ChatGPT didn't exist until 2022. The AI made up a source for a story from 5 years before it existed

slides.headline: NOBODY READ A SINGLE PAGE
slides.body: One report repeated the same fact three times in two pages, each with a different source. Other links in the reports led to broken pages or studies that don't exist

slides.headline: 5 MINUTES WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT ALL
slides.body: If a billion-dollar firm missed this, imagine what's slipping past your business. A single 5-minute check would have caught every error in all four reports

slides.headline: TWO MORE FIRMS ALREADY GOT CAUGHT
slides.body: EY and KPMG already pulled reports for the same thing. Follow, you'll want to see who's next. Send this to whoever lets ChatGPT write everything for them

caption:
Swipe to see how PwC got caught with ChatGPT links still in their own research reports 👀

PwC published at least four AI-written research reports between 2024 and 2026, one had a chatgpt.com tracking link in the footnotes, another cited a teenager's Medium blog with 280 followers as the sole source for a JPMorgan story, that JPMorgan project actually happened in 2017 before ChatGPT existed, one report repeated the same statistic three times in two pages with three different sources, other links led to broken pages or studies that don't exist in any journal, EY and KPMG also pulled papers for the same reason

The biggest consulting firms on earth are the ones cutting corners with AI the hardest. They charge millions to be the smartest people in the room and can't even read their own work before publishing.
